headline: Medium risk: shared network-egress automation can leak or misroute data, while direct prompt-injection pathways are not evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between Plane and Prefect, and neither profile shows a default parser for the other’s outputs. Plane has no browser and no filesystem write; Prefect only calls the GitHub API. With only docs-level evidence, a prompt-injection bridge is not established.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Plane content into Prefect task text, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared MCP, clipboard, or message queue is added, reassess for prompt injection.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting untrusted task text between systems.
Disable any shared clipboard or queue integration.
Add a review step before Prefect consumes Plane-generated text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and Plane touches files, images, hyperlinks, notes, issues, and tasks while Prefect handles workflow metadata. Even without a documented shared workspace, any operator-bridged transfer of Plane artifacts into Prefect can expose sensitive project data to outbound APIs.
conditions: IF Plane file uploads are forwarded into Prefect tasks, sensitive content can leave the original workspace.
IF both agents are authenticated to the same external service, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Restrict Plane uploads to non-sensitive files.
Do not pass raw attachments into Prefect flows.
Use separate service accounts for each agent.
Turn on outbound request logging for both agents.
Review any integration that syncs tasks or metadata between them.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plane cannot write the filesystem and Prefect exposes only API access, so direct write-write contention is not shown. The main overlap is broad network egress, which can still create coordination issues if both are pointed at the same external endpoints, but the profiles do not show shared mutable storage or locks.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to mutate the same external API resource, conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator adds shared writable storage, reassess for write contention.
mitigations: Assign distinct API credentials per agent.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same external object.
Add simple retry/backoff on 409 or 429 responses.
Document ownership of each mutable resource.
Use a lock or queue if a shared backend is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane can emit issues, tasks, and notes that Prefect could plausibly consume as workflow metadata, but no verification step is documented. Prefect’s orchestration role means a mistaken Plane output could cascade into downstream automation if operators wire the pair together, though this is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Prefect ingests Plane-generated tasks without human review, errors can propagate downstream.
IF Plane content is treated as authoritative workflow input, cascading mistakes become more likely.
mitigations: Require human approval before Prefect runs from Plane data.
Validate Plane fields against a schema before use.
Limit Prefect to read-only consumption of Plane outputs.
Add a checksum or provenance tag to transferred records.
Reject tasks lacking an explicit reviewer.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either open-source project, so compliance risk is limited to generic policy drift. Because both profiles are docs-only and the pairwise compliance pathway is not specified, the other agent is not separately implicated beyond the absence of evidence.
conditions: IF either deployment routes regulated data to a region or vendor not approved by policy, compliance risk increases.
IF retention settings differ across the two deployments, reassess.
mitigations: Confirm both deployments’ data residency settings.
Align retention and deletion policies.
Avoid regulated data until a DPA is in place.
Record which system stores each data class.
Review vendor terms before enabling sync.
